description: Four-track phrase sequencer, 32 steps to a sequence, 64 sequences to a track and 99 phrases to a song, each track separately clocked and edited

params.text: Chooses which phrase of the song is being edited, in song mode only
Chooses the sequence being played and edited, or in song mode the sequence number the current phrase calls up
Starts and stops all four tracks; there is one run state for the whole module
Copies the current sequence, or the chosen part of it, into the buffer; in song mode it copies phrases instead
Writes the buffer into the current sequence from the edit head, or into the song in song mode
Returns every track to the first step of its sequence or of its song
Sets the octave of the step at the edit head; the lit button is the octave that step holds
Turns the gate of the step at the edit head on or off
Turns on portamento from the previous step's voltage into this one; the slide time is set on the CV2 display, 1 being a whole clock period
Moves the edit head on to the next step after each write, so a run of notes can be entered one after another
Sets the order the steps are played in, or in song mode the order of the phrases: forward, reverse, ping-pong, pendulum, brownian, random, track A's positions, or each one once
Sets the track's clock resolution, which is what allows the advanced gate types, and its clock delay of 0 to 99 pulses; a reset is needed before a new delay takes effect
Opens transposing all 32 steps of the sequence or rotating the steps within its length, with the amount turned in on the sequence knob
Turns on probability for that step's gate, so the gate reaches the output only some of the time; the chance is set on the CV2 display, 0 to 1
Ties the step at the edit head to the step before it, so one note is held across both
Sets how many steps or phrases SEL and COPY-PASTE work on: four, eight, or a custom range picked out by clicking
Moves the edit head to that step, its lamps showing the gate and whether the step is picked out; while the length or repeat setting is open, clicking a step sets the length there and then
Steps back through the four tracks, choosing the one every edit acts on
Steps forward through the four tracks, choosing the one every edit acts on
Sets the value shown on the CV2 display for the step at the edit head: its second control voltage, its gate probability, or its slide time
Extends every edit across a run of steps, as many of them as the 4/8/CUST switch chooses
Applies every edit to all four tracks at once
In sequence mode it sets how many steps the sequence plays; in song mode it sets how many times the current phrase repeats, 0 to 99, where 0 skips the phrase
Marks the current phrase as the first one the song plays, for working on one section of a long song
Marks the current phrase as the last one the song plays
Switches the keyboard between entering notes and entering gate types
Makes the edit heads follow the run heads, so the step being edited is the step being played
Steps the CV2 display through the three things it can hold for a step: the second control voltage, the gate probability and the slide time
Switches the whole sequencer between editing and playing single sequences and building a song out of numbered phrases

inputs.text: A trigger here writes whatever is arriving at the CV inputs into the step at the edit head; an input with no cable is left out of the write
The pitch written into that track's current step when a trigger reaches WRITE
A trigger here returns every track to the first step of its sequence or of its song
Advances that track one step per pulse; with no cable patched, the track runs on the clock of the track before it
A trigger here starts and stops all four tracks

outputs.text: The pitch of the step that track has reached, at a volt per octave
The second control voltage of the step that track has reached, 0-10V, for accents or velocity
The gate of the step that track has reached

notes: each track has its own clock input, and a track with nothing patched to its CLK input runs on the clock of the track before it, so one cable into track A's CLK clocks all four
right-clicking a key of the onboard keyboard enters the note and moves on to the next step; holding ctrl while right-clicking carries the current gate type over as well
with the mouse over the sequence display, a sequence number can be typed on the computer keyboard, two key presses within one second reading as a two-digit number
in song mode, with the mouse over the sequence display, the space bar moves on to the next phrase
menu: Poly merge into track A outputs — None, Track B, Tracks B and C, or Tracks B, C and D; merged tracks become extra channels of track A's outputs and their own outputs hold 0V
CV2 mode — reads the CV2 value as Volts at 0.05V resolution, as 0-127 numbered levels, or as Notes, which rescales the CV2 outputs to semitones
CV2 bipolar — changes the CV2 outputs from 0-10V to -5V to 5V
Seq CV in level — sets how the SEQ# CV inputs on the expander are read: 0-10V across the 64 sequences, the note voltages C2-D7#, or Trig-Incr, where a trigger steps to the next sequence
Single shot song — plays the song once instead of repeating it, stopped by the track chosen from Off, Track A, Track B, Track C and Track D
Reset on run — returns every track to the start each time the sequencer is started
Retrigger gates on reset — holds the gate outputs low for 1ms after a reset so a trigger-sensitive target fires again; the choices are No, Yes, and Only when Run cable is unconnected
Hold tied notes — keeps the gate high across a run of tied steps; with it off only the first step of the run carries a gate
AutoStep write bounded by seq length — stops a write autostepping past the last step of the sequence
AutoSeq when writing via CV inputs — moves on to the next sequence when a write runs off the end of the current one, which turns the sequencer into a long CV recorder
Add expander (10HP right side) — places the FOUNDRY-X expander against the right edge of this module
Portable sequence — holds Copy sequence and Paste sequence, which move the selected sequence between this module and other sequencers; it can be used in SEQ mode only
